_comment: Guided tour for the phasor calculator. Steps point at real controls; the user edits them. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What this calculator is for
steps.text:
Before reading a phasor plot of real data you need to know where the things you expect would land: a donor at its unquenched lifetime, the same donor under FRET, a mixture of two species. This tool draws that geometry. It needs no data.

Six steps. You change the values; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Set the frequency first
steps.text: Everything on the plot moves with ω = 2π · frequency · harmonic. Use the laser repetition rate of your instrument — not the TCSPC window.

await.hint: Type your laser repetition rate (MHz) and press Enter.

steps.title: Place the lifetimes you expect
steps.text: Each lifetime becomes a tick on the semicircle, with an iso-phase ray and an iso-modulation arc through it. Their g and s appear under Results.

await.hint: Enter a comma-separated list of lifetimes in ns and press Enter.

steps.title: Spread them with a harmonic
steps.text: Lifetimes resolve best where nωτ ≈ 1. If yours crowd against (1, 0) on the right, a higher harmonic spreads them out.

steps.title: Add the FRET trajectory
steps.text: The path a mono-exponential donor takes as FRET shortens it from τD0 towards zero lifetime. A mix of FRET and donor-only molecules lies inside the circle, on the chord between the two points.

await.hint: Tick FRET trajectory, then set Donor τ0 below it.

steps.title: A two-species mixture
steps.text: Copy two lifetimes' g and s from Results into g1/s1 and g2/s2, tick Mixing region and move Fraction c1. The mixture point slides along the chord in proportion to the photon fraction, not the amplitude.

steps.title: Look at the plot
steps.text: The drawing lives in its own tab. Short lifetimes on the right, long on the left; anything inside the arc is multi-exponential.
